title: Entergy Mississippi helps advance Museum Trail with Capitol Green Connector milestone
summary: Entergy Mississippi helped advance the Museum Trail with the completion of the Capitol Green Connector, supported by company grants and employee volunteers.
body_markdown:
Ed Gardner, vice president of economic development for Entergy Mississippi, joins community leaders and supporters to celebrate completion of the Capitol Green Connector, the first phase of the Downtown Museum Trail.


The Museum Trail in Jackson, Mississippi, is a growing six-mile urban greenway that connects neighborhoods, parks, museums, business districts and cultural destinations. Following a historic railroad corridor, it supports walking, bicycling, recreation, public health and economic development while creating a connected network of public spaces.


The Museum Trail is made possible through public and private partnerships aiming to build a better Mississippi. Entergy Mississippi supports the Museum Trail through a grant from its Environmental Initiatives Fund.


This morning, Ed Gardner, vice president of economic development for Entergy Mississippi, joined community leaders and supporters to celebrate completion of the Capitol Green Connector, the first phase of the Downtown Museum Trail.


This new segment connects the Two Mississippi Museums, Old Capitol Museum, historic GM&O Depot, Hall & Mal’s, and surrounding destinations through a landscaped pedestrian path and bicycle corridor.


“This was a really important investment for us, for this community,” said Gardner. “We recently celebrated the 25th anniversary of the Environmental Initiatives Fund, where Entergy shareholders have invested $46 million in projects to protect natural resources, reduce emissions, restore habitats and strengthen community resilience.”


In 2025 alone, the EIF provided $1 million in shareholder-funded support to 11 partner organizations working in areas such as wetland restoration, tree planting, biodiversity education and green infrastructure development.


In August, Entergy volunteers helped plant trees, grasses and shrubs along the Capitol Green Connector as construction continued on the trail segment that opened today.


The volunteer event was held a stone’s throw from Entergy Mississippi’s Distribution Operation Center on South Street in downtown Jackson as construction continued on the section of the trail that was opened today.


The Museum Trail project complements Entergy’s broader environmental commitments, which include coastal restoration partnerships, conservation programs and the company’s long-term goal of achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050.


The Museum Trail work is part of a broader strategy to help our customers and communities thrive.


In recent years, Entergy and its partners have planted or distributed more than 337,000 trees and contributed thousands of volunteer hours across its service area, including tree planting efforts along the Museum Trail earlier this year.


The Museum Trail creates valuable urban greenspace that strengthens community connections, enhances quality of life and beautifies the area. It also makes Jackson more attractive to residents, visitors and businesses while helping manage stormwater, support biodiversity, improve air quality and reduce urban heat.


The next phase, the Arts District Connector, will extend the trail through Downtown Jackson, linking the Mississippi Museum of Art, Thalia Mara Hall, Planetarium, Jackson Convention Complex, and other cultural destinations. Future phases will expand west toward Jackson State University, north toward the Mississippi Farmers Market, and south toward Riverfront Park on the Pearl River.
